subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should OpenClaw keep first-entry default-agent selection when `agents.list` is first populated, or require an explicit default/prompt when that would displace implicit `main`?
rationale: The viable fixes intentionally change documented routing semantics, warning behavior, or config-write UX, and automation should not choose that product/security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require explicit default before displacement
options.body: Keep runtime compatibility but make config-write/setup/doctor flows warn or fail when first-time `agents.list` has no `default: true` and existing `main` state would be displaced.

options.title: Warn but keep first-entry fallback
options.body: Preserve current routing semantics and add high-visibility diagnostics so operators can add explicit `main` themselves.

options.title: Auto-preserve implicit main
options.body: Materialize or select `main` as default when existing main state is detected, accepting a behavior change for first-entry-only configs.

recommendation.title: Require explicit default before displacement
recommendation.body: Keep runtime compatibility but make config-write/setup/doctor flows warn or fail when first-time `agents.list` has no `default: true` and existing `main` state would be displaced.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the multi-agent routing/default behavior and is the strongest history signal for the product/security policy choice.
